issues.legal_issue: Striking out a tenant’s defence for failure to comply with a rent-deposit order bars the tenant from resisting eviction on the ground that the landlords are only co-sharers and cannot maintain the suit alone.
material_facts: The respondent acknowledged that he was a tenant under the appellants and had paid rent to them, recognising them as landlords.
The respondent contended that other co-sharers were also landlords and that the appellants could not alone seek eviction.
After the respondent failed to comply with an order to deposit arrears and future rent, the trial court struck out his defence against eviction.
The trial court then heard the eviction suit ex parte and decreed eviction; the first appellate court affirmed the decree.
issues.conclusion: The co-sharer contention was a defence raised in the respondent’s capacity as a tenant, not a denial of the landlord–tenant relationship. It was therefore struck out along with his other tenant-related defences, and the ex parte hearing and eviction decree were valid. The appeal was allowed and the High Court’s judgment was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 11A of the Bihar Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1947, striking out a tenant’s defence against eviction for failure to comply with a rent-deposit order removes all defences raised in the tenant’s capacity as a tenant. A claim that the plaintiffs are only co-sharer landlords and cannot alone maintain eviction does not, where the tenant recognises them as landlords, deny the landlord–tenant relationship. The Court distinguished Mahabir Ram v. Shiva Shanker Prasad, AIR 1968 Patna 415, where the tenant denied the plaintiffs’ title and claimed title in himself.

rule.if: eviction_suit_pending and tenant_admitted_landlord_relation and tenant_challenged_landlords_as_only_co_sharers and tenant_failed_to_comply_with_rent_deposit_order and tenant_defence_struck_out

predicates.eviction_suit_pending: A landlord brought a suit seeking to evict a tenant.
predicates.tenant_admitted_landlord_relation: The tenant acknowledged the plaintiffs as landlords, including by paying rent to them.
predicates.tenant_challenged_landlords_as_only_co_s: The tenant argued that other co-sharers were also landlords and that the plaintiffs could not alone maintain the eviction suit.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_comply_with_rent_deposi: The tenant failed to comply with a court order to deposit rent.
predicates.tenant_defence_struck_out: The court struck out the tenant’s defence against eviction after the tenant failed to comply with the deposit order.

issues.definition: When a tenant in an eviction suit recognises the plaintiffs as landlords, contests their ability to sue alone because they are only co-sharers, and has the defence struck out after failing to comply with a rent-deposit order, the tenant-related defences are barred after striking out.
